s: Columnar OLAP monster: billions of rows scanned/aggregated in milliseconds for realtime analytics.
w: Column-oriented storage compresses sparse numeric/time data massively; vectorized execution processes batches SIMD-style. MergeTree family tables sort/partition data; materialized views pre-aggregate continuously. Inserts batch efficiently; updates rare by design. Distributed tables shard/replicate across nodes.
use: Product analytics dashboards over billions of events (funnels, cohorts)
Realtime ad-tech bidding stats and reporting
Observability backends (logs/traces at scale - Uber LogHouse, SigNoz)
avoid: Row-level OLTP updates/deletes (mutual exclusivity with design strengths)
Small data (<millions rows) where postgres GROUP BY is fine

pat.d: Kafka -> ClickHouse materialized views -> instant dashboards.

pits: Too-many-parts insert errors - batch inserts (≥1k rows/sec guidance)
Unbounded cardinality dims melt memory - cap dictionaries/buckets
tips: Why columnar wins analytics: only read needed columns + compress similar data together
